title: Minimal-polynomial spectral radius on a finite product of fields
statement: Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value $|\cdot|$, let $I$ be a nonempty finite set, and for each $j\in I$ let $L_j/K$ be a finite field extension. Give $P=\prod_{j\in I}L_j$ its coordinatewise $K$-algebra structure. For an element $x$ of $P$ or of one of the $L_j$, write its monic minimal polynomial over $K$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] as $p_x(Z)=Z^{d_x}+\sum_{i=1}^{d_x}a_{x,i}Z^{d_x-i}$ and define $s(x)=\max_{1\le i\le d_x}|a_{x,i}|^{1/i}$. (All these minimal polynomials have positive degree.) Then, for every $x=(x_j)_{j\in I}\in P$, $$s(x)=\max_{j\in I}s(x_j).$$ No completeness of $K$ or separability of the extensions is required.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 5.3.3/4, first paragraph, printed p.217 (scan PDF p.223), finite-product spectral maximum formula; general spectral-polynomial interpretation in Section 3.1.2. Primary scan read 2026-10-25; archival literature copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $p=p_x$, $p_j=p_{x_j}$, and $Q=\prod_{j\in I}p_j$. Each $L_j$ and the nontrivial finite product $P$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-algebra: combine finite spanning sets using the coordinate inclusions. By [lem-trf-finite-algebra-minpoly-properties], $p,p_j$ are monic of positive degree and vanish at their respective elements. Evaluation is coordinatewise, so $p(x_j)=0$ for every $j$, while $Q(x_j)=0$ since its $j$-th factor vanishes. Thus $Q(x)=0$. The divisibility clause of the same node gives $p_j\mid p$ for every $j$ and $p\mid Q$. No assertion that the polynomials $p_j$ are distinct or coprime is needed.

source.place: minpoly.dvd, lines 69-77, applied to coordinatewise evaluation; monicity and integrality clauses supplied by the cited node.

proof.text: For any monic polynomial $f=Z^d+\sum_{i=1}^d b_iZ^{d-i}$ put $s(f)=\max_{1\le i\le d}|b_i|^{1/i}$, and put $s(1)=0$. Fix $r>0$ and use $G_r$ from [lem-trf-polynomial-weighted-gauss-multiplicative]. Comparing each coefficient with the leading coefficient gives $G_r(f)\ge r^d$ and $G_r(f)=r^d$ if and only if $|b_i|r^{d-i}\le r^d$ for all $i$, equivalently $s(f)\le r$. If monic $f$ divides monic $h$, write $h=fg$. Leading coefficients and degrees show that $g$ is monic and $\deg h=\deg f+\deg g$. Whenever $s(h)\le r$, multiplicativity gives $G_r(f)G_r(g)=r^{\deg h}$; together with $G_r(g)\ge r^{\deg g}>0$ this implies $G_r(f)\le r^{\deg f}$. Hence $s(f)\le r$. Letting $r>s(h)$ vary gives $s(f)\le s(h)$; if this failed, the midpoint of the two nonnegative numbers would be a positive $r$ contradicting the bound.

source.place: Polynomial.gaussNorm and Polynomial.gaussNorm_mul, lines 49-50 and 276-279; elementary coefficient comparison and application to minimal polynomials.

proof.text: Let $M=\max_{j\in I}s(p_j)$. For every real $r>M$ one has $r>0$ and $G_r(p_j)=r^{\deg p_j}$ by the coefficient criterion in step 2. Applying [lem-trf-polynomial-weighted-gauss-multiplicative] repeatedly along the finite product yields $G_r(Q)=\prod_jG_r(p_j)=r^{\sum_j\deg p_j}=r^{\deg Q}$. The criterion gives $s(Q)\le r$ for every $r>M$, hence $s(Q)\le M$ by the same midpoint argument. Now step 1 and the monic-divisor bound in step 2 give $s(p)\le s(Q)\le M$ and $s(p_j)\le s(p)$ for every $j$. Taking the finite maximum proves $M\le s(p)$ and therefore $s(x)=s(p)=M=\max_js(x_j)$. Positivity of degrees, including $x=0$, came from step 1; no extension of the absolute value, completeness, or separability was used.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NS-b311ca4c9 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item and both new nodes in full. The item statement is unchanged. Step 1: coordinatewise evaluation gives p_j | p and p | Q = prod p_j, and no coprimality is used. Step 2: G_r(f) >= r^d, and G_r(f) = r^d iff s(f) <= r. For monic f | h, the quotient g is monic, and multiplicativity gives s(f) <= s(h), including the cases s(h) = 0 and s(1) = 0. Step 3: taking r > M avoids r = 0, and s(p_j) <= s(p) <= s(Q) <= M. I tested |I| = 1, x = 0, repeated p_j, a trivial absolute value and inseparable minimal polynomials; all hold. lem-trf-polynomial-weighted-gauss-multiplicative matches Mathlib GaussNorm.lean exactly: gaussNorm at 49-50, the AbsoluteValue / IsNonarchimedean / 0 < c section at 219-221, gaussNorm_mul at 276. It is not a duplicate of lem-trf-tate-gauss-multiplicative, which is weight 1 on restricted series and cannot be rescaled to weight r without some c in K with |c| = r. lem-trf-finite-algebra-minpoly-properties matches IsIntegral.of_finite (:64), minpoly.monic/aeval/natDegree_pos (Basic.lean 54/89/192, with Nontrivial B) and minpoly.dvd (Field.lean:69). An rg -L search of the DAG for minpoly, minimal-polynomial divisibility, monic divisors and Gauss norm found no duplicate. The BGR scan is absent from literature/ and is flagged WANTED; proof_origin is agent and rests only on the checked Mathlib inputs. No SGA is cited. No fixes.
